title: AccountabilityBinding
description: Binds a RUNNING capability (a PurposeTask / promoted artifact_key) to the human party who OWNS ITS OUTCOMES in production — accountability designed BEFORE deployment, not discovered during failure. Distinct from HumanApprovalReceipt, which is a point-in-time approval of a boundary-expanding CHANGE: this is the ONGOING answer to 'who owns the outcome when the agent acts', carrying the authority to pause/rollback and an ordered escalation path for when an outcome goes wrong. A capability serving at autonomy above its ceiling without an active binding is a governance violation. Reuses the approver_role vocabulary and REFERENCES the approval/promotion records rather than duplicating them.

subject_key.description: the capability the owner is accountable for: an artifact_key / PurposeTask id — ongoing, not a one-time change

accountable_owner.description: the party who owns the OUTCOME (a role or an id) — the single answer to 'who owns the outcome when the agent acts'

authority.description: what the owner may do BEFORE something breaks — human authority to prevent, not just observe

escalation_path.description: ordered roles to escalate to on incident/failure (reuses HumanApprovalReceipt.approver_role)

autonomy_ceiling.description: max adaptation-ladder level this capability may run at without a fresh HumanApprovalReceipt; L4/L5 (ENDS) are human-only

on_failure.description: the automatic action when an outcome breaches its guardrail, before the escalation is answered

linked_approval_ids.description: HumanApprovalReceipt ids that authorized this capability's boundary (composition, not duplication)

linked_promotion_id.description: the PromotionRecord that put this capability into service
